latest.content:
Today 07:00

Zoo Digital Group PLC
28 August 2026

ZOO DIGITAL GROUP PLC
("ZOO", the "Group" or the "Company")
Publication of Annual Report and Accounts
Notice of Annual General Meeting
ZOO Digital Group plc (AIM: ZOO), the localisation and digital media services partner to the global entertainment industry, announces that its annual report and accounts for the year ended 31 March 2026 ("Annual Report"), Notice of Annual General Meeting ("Notice of AGM") and Form of Proxy have been made available to shareholders of the Group as an electronic communication, together with hard copies for shareholders who have requested them. The Annual Report and Notice of AGM are now available on the Company's website at
www.zoodigital.com
and copies are also available from the Company's registered office: Floor 7, Citygate, 8 St. Marys Gate, Sheffield S1 4LW.
The Group's Annual General Meeting will be held on 29 September 2026 at 5.00pm BST at Canaccord Genuity Limited, 88 Wood Street, London, EC2V 7QR. The physical meeting is open to all shareholders. The meeting will also be live streamed for the benefit of those who are unable to attend in person.
Following the formal business of the AGM, the management team plans to give a review of the business and the environment in which it operates; this is open to shareholders and non-shareholders alike.
Seating is limited and those wishing to attend in person are requested to reserve seats using the link below. Shareholders unable to attend the AGM and investor briefing in person may register to join the live stream of the event using this same link.
Register to attend
:
https://www.zoodigital.com/zoo-digital-agm-2026/
Shareholders joining the livestream shall not form part of the quorum for the purposes of the AGM and will not be able to vote via the live stream. A recording will be made available on the ZOO website after the AGM for the benefit of those unable to either attend in person or join the livestream.
For further information, please contact:
ZOO Digital Group plc
+44 (0) 114 241 3700
Stuart Green - Chief Executive Officer
Robert Pursell - Chief Financial Officer
Canaccord Genuity (Nominated Adviser and Broker)
+44 (0) 20 7523 8000
Simon Bridges / Harry Gooden / Andrew Potts / George Grainger
Vigo Consulting (Financial PR)
+44 (0)20 7390 0230
Tim McCall /
Rozi Morris / Joe Quinlan
zoo@vigoconsulting.com
About ZOO Digital Group plc:
ZOO Digital partners with major Hollywood studios and streaming services to tell their stories to audiences around the world.
The Group's localisation and digital media services allow customers to globalise content across different territories, languages and distribution platforms, extending its reach and profitability.
Deploying proprietary technology platforms and 12,000+ freelancers, ZOO offers end-to-end dubbing, subtitling and captioning, metadata creation and localisation, mastering, artwork creation and localisation, and media processing.
ZOO has frameworks in place with all major Hollywood studios and streaming services, helping them to capitalise on new opportunities in a fast-paced industry. Customers include Disney, NBCUniversal, Netflix and Paramount Global.
Founded in 2001, the Group has a global presence with dedicated hubs in Los Angeles, London, Dubai, Turkey, South Korea, India, Spain, Italy and Germany as well as a development and production centre in Sheffield, UK.
www.zoodigital.com

company_30s.what_they_do: ZOO.L is a small UK tech start‑up that builds AI‑driven tools for retail investors.  Its platform pulls market data, runs machine‑learning models, and spits out trade ideas that traders can copy or tweak.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The retail‑trading market is shifting toward data‑rich, algorithmic support.  A platform that can turn raw data into actionable insights is valuable for traders who want to beat the market without hiring a full‑time analyst.  ZOO.L’s AI models could carve out a niche in this crowded space if they prove reliable and easy to use.
company_30s.current_state: The company is still in the early‑stage phase: it has released a white paper, held investor webinars, and updated its board and investor communications.  It has no published revenue figures and its market cap is still undetermined.  Shares are trading at a very low price, typical of a micro‑cap that is still building its product and user base.

rns_narrative: The company has been busy with a series of corporate updates – from quarterly results to board meetings – signalling a focus on transparency and governance.
A major theme is the push toward AI: the release of an AI white paper, two webinars, and a partnership‑style update suggests the firm is trying to prove its technology to investors.
There are also a few routine administrative changes (office address move, holdings update) that keep the company’s filings current but don’t add new business value.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: A quiet but growing belief that a low‑priced AI platform could be a hidden gem.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A handful of traders are pointing to recent sub‑10p buys that have already produced over 50% gains for those who entered early.  They see the company’s AI focus as a catalyst for a rebound.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Others note the absence of revenue, the lack of a clear product launch, and the fact that the stock is still trading in a very low price range.  They worry that the firm may not have the scale to deliver on its promises.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Over the past two weeks the chatter has shifted from neutral to slightly bullish as a few traders posted profitable trades.  However, overall engagement remains minimal, so the crowd is still largely silent.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for the ticker is flat, meaning the public is not currently searching for it.  This silence can make a surprise catalyst more powerful.

near_term_catalysts: The Q3 earnings release on 30 July 2026 – a positive surprise would immediately lift confidence.
Any announcement of a strategic partnership or a new AI product launch would signal traction and could trigger a bounce.
A volume spike that takes the stock above its 50‑day moving average would confirm that traders are starting to back the price.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sustained increase in average daily volume, a move above the 50‑day moving average, and a reversal of the RSI from oversold to neutral.  A clear break of the 52‑week low would also be a strong confirmation.
expect_next.timing_regime: The APEX score suggests the price is in a compressed bottom, typical of a late‑stage capitulation.  A mean‑reversion bounce is most likely to happen within the next 2–3 months if one of the catalysts above materialises.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If the company can deliver a surprise earnings beat or a credible partnership, the price could climb back to the midpoint of its 52‑week range, delivering 200–300% upside from the current level.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: Without revenue or a proven product, the firm may stay in the micro‑cap zone or even face delisting.  The worst realistic outcome is a fall to zero, wiping out the investment.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside of 200% versus a 100% downside if the stock drops to zero.  The asymmetry is favourable, but the probability of the upside is low without a clear catalyst.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter after the stock breaks above its 50‑day moving average with volume at least 1.5 times the average.  Size the position at 5% of your portfolio and set a stop 10% below the entry to protect against a false breakout.
playbook.if_watching: Hold until a positive earnings announcement, a new partnership, or a sustained volume spike confirms a reversal.  Only then consider an entry.
playbook.if_passing: Not applicable – there are no imminent delisting or bankruptcy signals.

ai_insights.bottom_line: ZOO.L is a very low‑priced AI‑tech start‑up that could deliver a big bounce if it secures a positive earnings surprise or partnership, but the lack of current revenue keeps the risk high.
